statement:
Build a Tetris game as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo root.

Requirements:
- A playfield 10 columns wide and 20 rows tall. Row 0 is the top row.
- The seven tetrominoes: `I`, `O`, `T`, `S`, `Z`, `J`, `L`. Give each one its own colour.
- A piece spawns at the top and falls one row at a time under gravity.
- When a piece can no longer fall, it locks in place and the next piece spawns.
- The player can move the falling piece left and right, soft drop it (one row down), and hard
  drop it. A hard drop sends the piece straight down to the lowest position it can reach and

title: Build Tetris game in single HTML file
statement: Build a Tetris game as a single static HTML file named `index.html` in the repo root with a 10×20 playfield, seven tetrominoes, gravity, locking, player movement, hard drop, and score/level/lines display.
acceptance: index.html file created with inline CSS and JavaScript
Playfield renders as 200 DOM cells (10 columns × 20 rows) with data-testid and data-row/data-col attributes
Seven tetrominoes (I, O, T, S, Z, J, L) each have distinct CSS colours via [data-piece] rules
Piece spawns at top and falls one row per gravity step
When piece locks, next piece spawns automatically
Player can move falling piece left/right with arrow keys
Soft drop (↓) moves piece down one row
Hard drop (Space) sends piece to lowest position and locks immediately
Score, level, and lines cleared display in DOM with correct data-testid attributes
Initial state: score 0, level 1, lines 0
sub_requirements: Playfield structure and rendering
Tetromino definitions and colours
Gravity and piece locking
Player controls (movement, soft drop, hard drop)
Score/level/lines display
Constraint: single file, inline code, synchronous DOM updates

title: Add rotation, and settle how a piece locks.
statement:
Add rotation, and settle how a piece locks.

- The player can rotate the falling piece clockwise. Add `"rotateCW"` to the actions
  `window.__tetris.input(action)` accepts.
- A rotation must never put the piece outside the board or on top of a locked cell. If the
  rotated shape does not fit where it is, the game may shift it sideways to make room. If
  nothing works, refuse the rotation and leave the piece exactly as it was.

Locking rule — this is a decision, keep it for the rest of the project:
- A gravity step moves the falling piece down one row. If it cannot move down, that step
  counts...

title: Add line clears and scoring.
statement:
Add line clears and scoring.

- When a piece locks, every full row is removed and everything above it drops down.
- Count the rows removed in `lines` and show it.

Scoring model — this is a decision, keep it for the rest of the project:
- Points for a clear depend on how many rows go at once:
  1 row = 100, 2 rows = 300, 3 rows = 500, 4 rows = 800.
- That number is multiplied by the current level.
- Soft drop scores 1 point for each cell the piece moves down under the player's control.
- Hard drop scores 2 points for each cell the piece drops.

The reason for the table: clearing rows together ...

title: Line clears and scoring
statement: When a piece locks, full rows are removed and rows above drop down; scoring follows a level-dependent multiplier model with points for line clears, soft drops, and hard drops.
acceptance: Full rows are removed when a piece locks
Rows above a cleared row drop down
lines counter counts and displays removed rows
Clear points are 100/300/500/800 for 1/2/3/4 rows cleared at once, multiplied by current level
Soft drop scores 1 point per cell moved under player control
Hard drop scores 2 points per cell dropped
Clearing rows together always scores more than clearing the same rows in smaller splits (verified by test)
sub_requirements: Remove full rows and drop remaining rows
Count and display lines cleared
Apply scoring multiplier based on number of rows cleared simultaneously
Score soft drop and hard drop player actions
Verify scoring rule: clearing together beats clearing separately

title: Two additions.
statement:
Two additions.

Next-piece preview:
- Show the next **three** upcoming pieces, soonest first.
- `data-testid="next-piece"` — the preview container.
- `data-testid="next-piece-item"` — one upcoming piece in the preview, in order, each carrying
  `data-piece="I|O|T|S|Z|J|L"`.
- Colour-code each preview piece by its type, using the colour that piece has on the board.

Game over:
- When a newly spawned piece has nowhere to go, the game ends.
- `data-testid="game-over"` — shown when the game is over.
- `window.__tetris.getState().status` becomes `"gameover"`.
- Once the game is over, gravity steps ...

title: Next-piece preview and game-over state
statement: Show the next three upcoming pieces with colour coding, and end the game when a spawned piece cannot fit.
acceptance: Preview shows three next pieces in a `next-piece` container with `data-testid="next-piece"`
Each preview piece is a `next-piece-item` element with `data-testid="next-piece-item"` carrying `data-piece` attribute matching its type
Preview pieces are colour-coded by type using the same colour rules as board cells
Game-over element with `data-testid="game-over"` is shown when game ends
Game status becomes `"gameover"` when a newly spawned piece has nowhere to fit
Gravity steps and player actions do nothing once game is over
sub_requirements: Next-piece preview: show three upcoming pieces soonest first with colour coding
Game-over state: detect when spawn fails and set status to gameover, display game-over element

title: Players are complaining about the down key.
statement:
Players are complaining about the down key.

"I slam a piece down with the down arrow and it locks under my fingers before I can nudge it.
Tapping left or right at the bottom gives me a moment to think, but tapping down doesn't."

Fix that: a soft drop on a piece that is already resting on the stack should buy the player
the same breathing room a sideways move buys.

title: Soft drop on resting piece buys breathing room
statement: A soft drop on a piece that is already resting on the stack should restart the lock delay like a sideways move does.
acceptance: Soft drop on a resting piece restarts the lock delay
Soft drop on resting piece shares the same 3-restart budget as sideways moves
Soft drop on resting piece scores no points
sub_requirements: Restart lock delay when soft drop is used on resting piece
Share restart budget with sideways moves
Score nothing when soft dropping a resting piece

title: Three upcoming pieces is too much information — it turns the game into a plannin...
statement:
Three upcoming pieces is too much information — it turns the game into a planning exercise and
it crowds the panel. Show only the next piece.

Keep the colour-coding in the preview. That part works.

title: Show only the next piece in preview
statement: Show only the next piece in the preview panel instead of three upcoming pieces.
acceptance: PREVIEW_COUNT changed from 3 to 1 in code
Preview displays only the next piece in its colour
Multi-item preview code retained for future extensibility
getState().next still returns whole queue for backward compatibility with tests
sub_requirements: Reduce information displayed from three pieces to one
Maintain colour-coding in preview
Keep preview grid structure (4x2)

title: Two additions.
statement:
Two additions.

Levels and speed:
- The level starts at 1 and goes up by one for every 10 lines cleared. It never goes down.
- The higher the level, the faster gravity runs. The interval between gravity steps, in
  milliseconds, is `max(100, 1000 - (level - 1) * 100)`.
- `window.__tetris.getState()` gains `dropInterval` — that interval in milliseconds.
- `window.__tetris.tick(n)` is unchanged: it always advances exactly n gravity steps, whatever
  the level is.
- Add `window.__tetris.setLevel(n)` — sets the current level to n, for testing. Levelling from
  lines carries on from there, and the ...

title: Levels and hold
statement: Add level progression and hold mechanic to the Tetris game.
acceptance: Level starts at 1 and increments by 1 for every 10 lines cleared, never decreases
Gravity interval formula: max(100, 1000 - (level - 1) * 100) milliseconds
window.__tetris.getState() returns dropInterval property
window.__tetris.setLevel(n) sets current level for testing, levelling from lines continues
window.__tetris.input('hold') action available via C, Shift keys
Hold slot displays held piece or empty state
data-testid='hold-piece' element exists with data-piece attribute
One hold per piece: second hold refused until piece locks
Pieces from hold spawn at spawn position
sub_requirements: Level system: starts at 1, increases by 1 per 10 lines cleared, gravity interval decreases with level
Hold mechanic: one hold slot per piece with swap functionality

title: Bug report from a player:
statement:
Bug report from a player:

"I've been grinding at level 5. I set up a well, dropped an I piece down it and took four rows
at once — and it scored me less than the two-row clears I'd been getting, twice over. Four
rows in one go is the hardest thing in the game. It can't be worth less than doing it the
easy way."

Reproduce it and fix it.

title: Two additions.
statement:
Two additions.

Ghost piece:
- Show where the falling piece would land, as an outline at the bottom of the board.
- Ghost cells carry `data-ghost="true"`. They are not filled cells — leave their
  `data-filled` as `"false"`.
- `window.__tetris.getState()` gains `ghost` — the array of `[row, col]` cells the ghost
  occupies.

Pause:
- `data-testid="pause-btn"` — a button that pauses and resumes.
- `data-testid="paused-indicator"` — shown while the game is paused.
- `window.__tetris.getState().status` becomes `"paused"` while paused.
- Add `"pause"` to the actions `window.__tetris.input(action)`...

title: Ghost piece and pause feature
statement: Show where a falling piece would land as a ghost outline, and add a pause/resume button that freezes gravity and lock delay without granting extra time.
acceptance: Ghost cells appear at landing position with data-ghost="true" and data-filled="false"
getState().ghost returns array of [row, col] cells where piece lands
Pause button with data-testid="pause-btn" toggles pause state
Paused indicator with data-testid="paused-indicator" shown while paused
getState().status becomes "paused" while paused
input("pause") action toggles pause state
Pause accepts keyboard inputs: P, Shift+P, Escape
Gravity steps and player actions ignored while paused
Lock count, restarts, and remaining time preserved across pause/resume
sub_requirements: Ghost piece visualization at landing position
Pause and resume functionality
Lock delay preservation across pause cycles

title: Final pass.
statement:
Final pass.

Add keyboard controls:
- Left and Right arrows move the piece.
- Down arrow soft drops.
- Up arrow rotates clockwise.
- Space hard drops.
- C holds.
- P pauses and resumes.
- R starts a new game.

Add `data-testid="restart-btn"` — a button that starts a new game: empty board, score 0,
lines 0, level 1, running.

Then verify that nothing we built in earlier steps has broken, and fix anything that has.

title: Final pass: keyboard controls and restart button
statement: Add keyboard controls (arrow keys, space, C, P, R) and a restart button with test ID, verifying no earlier features broke.
acceptance: R key starts a new game from any state (paused or game over)
Restart button has data-testid='restart-btn'
Restart button empties board, sets score 0, lines 0, level 1, running state
Left/Right arrows, Down, Up, Space, C, P keys functional
Browser shortcuts (Cmd+R, Ctrl+R, etc.) still work
Held keys don't repeat pause or newGame actions
On-screen key list updated to show 'R new game'
No earlier features broken
sub_requirements: Add R key control for new game
Add restart-btn with data-testid attribute
Verify earlier features intact
